claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified for launch now based on aggregate readiness pass, clean severity-one rehearsal results, and public AI governance guidance, despite an unresolved enterprise refund workflow gap, an open legal disclosure question, and policy language treating named launch use cases as material.
decision_criteria: If admissible evidence shows the limitation was disclosed as required before launch, the verdict could improve.
If admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance covered the limitation before launch, the verdict could improve.
If admissible evidence shows the workflow was not actually a named launch use case or contractual customer segment, the materiality basis could weaken.
Without one of those showings, certification remains unsupported under the stated policy.
evidence_requests: Produce the final legal determination on whether this gap required disclosure for launch.
Produce the final model card or launch disclosure showing the material limitation was disclosed.
Produce the approved risk acceptance that explicitly covers this workflow gap before launch.
Produce the underlying evidence showing whether the affected workflow is a named launch use case or contractual commitment in scope of the policy.
specific_concerns: The controlling policy says a weakness is material if it affects a named launch use case or contractual customer segment, and the packet itself says the affected workflow is named in a renewal success plan.
The Actor cites no admissible evidence that the limitation was disclosed before launch or covered by approved risk acceptance, even though the policy requires one of those conditions.
The packet states legal review on disclosure is still open, which leaves a policy predicate unresolved at decision time.
Aggregate readiness and clean rehearsal results do not by themselves satisfy the disclosure or risk-acceptance requirement for a material limitation.
Public governance guidance is general and cannot override the case-specific release policy.
unsupported_claims: That the 4% traffic characterization is enough to treat the gap as non-material.
That documenting limitations and monitoring post-launch is sufficient absent evidence of required disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
